## Objects and normalizations

For positive integer indices n≤N, `P_N(s)=Σ a_n exp(−s log n)`. The abstract criterion has a₁=1. Define `M_N=max{n≤N:a_n≠0}` and `E_N(σ)=Σ|a_n|² n^(−2σ)`. The Bohr polynomial uses the prime-factorization vector of n and normalized product Haar probability on the finite prime torus. Its vertical substitution is `z_p=exp(−it log p)`.

`J_N(σ)=lim_{T→∞}(1/(2T))∫_{−T}^T log|P_N(σ+it)|dt`. Its second derivative is a positive distribution/Stieltjes measure. For every a<b, the source's multiplicity-weighted zero count on `a<Re s<b`, `|Im s|<T`, divided by 2T, tends to `(J′_N(b−)−J′_N(a+))/(2π)`. The total measure is `log M_N/(2π)`; `ν_N=J″_N/log M_N` is a probability when M_N>1. Do not identify this with a finite-height empirical measure without proving a separate limit.

For λ>0, the test polynomial `1+exp(−λs)` has Jessen potential `max(0,−λσ)`, second derivative `λδ₀` and zero frequency `λ/(2π)`. This catches sign and 2π errors. Totalized real logarithm at zero needs a null-set/integrability bridge, not a definitional shortcut.

## Theorem 2.2: exact assumptions and outputs

Fix α∈ℝ and `Q_N ⊆ {p prime : N/2<p≤N}`, with `#Q_N→∞`.

- H1: for every σ∈ℝ, `log E_N(σ)/(2 log N) → max(α−σ,0)`.
- H2: for every compact interval I⊂(−∞,α), there is K_I≥1 such that eventually in N, for every σ∈I and every p,q∈Q_N, the ratio `|a_p|p^(−σ)/(|a_q|q^(−σ))` is between K_I⁻¹ and K_I. In particular these coefficients are positive in modulus. With `B_N(σ)=Σ_{p∈Q_N}|a_p|²p^(−2σ)`, `log B_N/(2log N)→α−σ` locally uniformly below α.
- Conclusions: `J_N/log N→max(α−σ,0)` locally uniformly on **all ℝ**, and `ν_N` converges weakly to δ_α. Derive eventual `N/2<M_N≤N`, M_N>1 and `log M_N/log N→1` from the actual prime blocks. Do not assume these consequences as replacement hypotheses.

Weak convergence must reach bounded continuous test functions, with tightness and mass conservation proved. An equality only against compact smooth tests is an intermediate distributional result.

## Concrete applications

**Theorem 2.4 and Corollary 6.1:** a_n=1, α=1/2 and M_N=N. Prove every energy regime and ordinary dyadic prime asymptotic. For every ε>0 the normalized vertical density outside `|β−1/2|<ε` tends to zero, with the printed boundary-line convention made precise. Preserve `(2π/log N) lim_{T→∞} count/(2T)` followed by N→∞.

**Theorem 2.5 and Lemma 7.1:** fix positive q and any Dirichlet character χ modulo q. Here `M_N=max{n≤N:gcd(n,q)=1}`. Prove `|χ(n)|²=1` for coprime n and 0 otherwise, and coprime counting `φ(q)x/q+O_q(1)`. For σ<1/2 the energy main term is `(φ(q)/q)N^(1−2σ)/(1−2σ)` with lower-order remainder; at σ=1/2 it is `(φ(q)/q)log N+O_q(1)`; above 1/2 the sum is bounded. For N>2q every prime in (N/2,N] is coprime to q. Derive the support bound `N−q+1≤M_N≤N` and both theorem conclusions. Include q=1 and principal/imprimitive cases.

**Theorem 2.6, Lemma 8.1 and Corollary 8.2:** fixed normalized primitive holomorphic Hecke eigenform f, even k≥2, level Q, trivial character, non-CM. Its actual Fourier coefficients have a_f(1)=1, and `λ_f(n)=a_f(n)n^(−(k−1)/2)`. Rankin–Selberg gives `Σ_{n≤x}|λ_f(n)|²=c_f x+O_f(x^(3/5))`, c_f>0; partial summation gives all weighted energy regimes. Handle the vanishing derivative at σ=0, the logarithmic error threshold σ=3/10 and σ=1/2 separately where needed.

Deligne and Sato–Tate give real λ_f(p)∈[−2,2] at unramified primes with semicircle density `(1/(2π))√(4−x²)`. For η equal to the positive mass of `{1≤|x|≤2}`, the good primes in (N/2,N] have cardinality `(η/2+o(1))N/log N`; exclude p|Q. On each compact σ interval derive coefficient comparability (the source uses `2^(M_I+1)`) and locally uniform B_N asymptotics. The BLGG input is Corollary 7.1.7 with its own Hecke/automorphic normalization; a citation or generic eigenvalue sequence does not supply the bridge.

Apply Theorem 2.2 to λ_f to obtain concentration at 1/2. Prove `Σa_f(n)n^(−s)=Σλ_f(n)n^(−(s−(k−1)/2))`, then transport Jessen functions, zero multiplicities and measures to concentration at k/2. The level-one primitive/non-CM implications are now proved for the stated normalized eigenforms by `primitiveCuspFormLevelOne` and `nonCMPrimitiveCuspFormLevelOne`. The Rankin–Selberg, Deligne and Sato–Tate inputs remain OPEN and part of the whole-paper objective.

### Actual rescaled cusp traces and common-period Mellin identity — 7 October 2026

The original product-level cusp form is translated by the actual inverse diagonal matrix. The mixed subgroup has exactly the upper-right divisibility by a and lower-left divisibility by b; its real image is proved equal to the diagonal conjugate of Gamma0(ab), and it contains Gamma(ab). Restricting each genuine integral coset translate to the normal principal subgroup therefore supplies one common period ab. The finite sum retains every actual coset once. Its Petersson density is full-level invariant, so its horizontal square energy is one-periodic. Exact averaging over ab periods and actual Parseval identify that unit-interval integral with the complete finite family of q-expansion squares.

Every actual normalized period coefficient family has a proved linear mean. Summing the genuine finite family and convolving with the full-level principal square sequence preserves nonnegativity and the linear mean, giving absolute convergence for Re(s)>1. The exact Mellin transform has factor (4 pi / ab)^(-(s+k-1)) Gamma(s+k-1). Absolute Bochner integrability is proved by summable integral norms; no formal exchange of a divergent integral and series is used. The integer and projective coset domains have equal multiplicities because the mixed group absorbs the center, and diagonal transport of the original Gamma0 domain gives a second genuine domain for the same real projective group.

This is the actual coefficient and domain construction. The reflected lattice-cusp integral has not yet been identified with this coefficient series. That identification still needs the invariant completed-Eisenstein trace unfolding and the exact determinant/conductor factors. The general-level contour estimates and x^(3/5) conclusion remain OPEN. The already verified full-level Rankin–Selberg theorem and all weighted energy regimes remain intact. Deligne and unconditional Sato–Tate remain OPEN. No gate changes: 15/20 accepted.

### Actual local roots and all-prime Euler factors — 7 October 2026

The local roots are constructed from the original normalized Fourier coefficient as (lambda_p +/- sqrt(lambda_p^2-4))/2. Their trace is lambda_p and their product is one. Actual coefficient reality proves the exact equivalence between unit modulus of both roots and |lambda_p|<=2 at every unramified prime. This is a normalization equivalence: neither side is asserted without its missing arithmetic proof.

The proved absolute convergence of the original normalized square series and the elementary bound |lambda_n|<=|lambda_n|^2+1 imply absolute convergence of the actual first-power cusp Dirichlet series for Re(s)>1. Genuine coprime Hecke multiplicativity supplies its Euler product. Summing the actual good-prime recurrence gives 1/(1-lambda_p p^(-s)+p^(-2s)); summing the ramified geometric recurrence gives 1/(1-lambda_p p^(-s)). Their nonzero denominators follow from the convergent coefficient recurrences themselves. This all-prime product requires no Deligne premise and is not a separate assumed Euler-product object.

The finite trace sum over alpha_p^i beta_p^(r-i) is proved to satisfy the same determinant-one recurrence and hence equals the original lambda_f(p^r) at every good prime. The actual symmetric-power local Euler polynomial is the product of its r+1 spectral factors; its linear coefficient is -lambda_f(p^r), and the derivative at zero of its reciprocal is lambda_f(p^r). Unit local roots, if supplied, yield the precise prime-power bound r+1 and nonvanishing of these polynomials in the open unit disc. These statements include repeated-root cases and do not assume a diagonalization with distinct roots.
